models.description: Groups wards that look alike across complaints, resolution, water and waste. Unsupervised: there are no right answers to train against, so it describes patterns rather than predicting anything.

models.name: Complaint forecasts
models.method: Per family of series, the best of three simple methods by rolling backtest; 80% interval from that method's backtest errors
models.description: Predicts how many complaints will be registered in 2026, with a range. Built on ten yearly figures per series, so the ranges are wide on purpose.

methods.mean3: Average of the last three years
methods.trend: Straight-line trend over all earlier years

models.trained_on: Complaints registered 2016-2025; Praja Foundation 2026 report Tables 1, 39, 41, 43

models.name: Waste forecasts
models.method: Best of three simple methods by backtest on 2024 and 2025; 80% interval from that method's backtest errors
models.description: Predicts the tonnes of waste BMC will lift per day in 2026, for the city and each ward. Only five years are published, so it is tested on two years and the ranges are wide.

methods.mean3: Average of the last three years
methods.trend: Straight-line trend over all earlier years

models.trained_on: Waste lifted per day 2021-2025; Praja Foundation 2026 report Table 37

models.name: Air-quality forecast
models.method: Best of four seasonal methods by forecasting each whole year 2022-2025 from the years before it; 80% interval from that method's errors
models.description: Predicts Mumbai's average AQI for each month of 2026. Air quality follows a strong yearly cycle (worst in winter, best in the monsoon), so every method is built around that cycle.

methods.smean3: Same month, average of the last three years
methods.climatology: Same month, average of all earlier years
methods.profile: Seasonal shape of all earlier years, at last year's level

models.trained_on: Monthly average AQI 2016-2025 (120 months); Praja Foundation 2026 report Table 29
